steps.content: A few weeks later.
The massive sand ship cruises through the WhiteSands, a great black whale in a sea of dunes.
[Sand Ship Deck]
Milly stands on the deck, her eyes fixed on the horizon where a wall of leaden clouds has gathered, closing in on them.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Sand Ship 4A calling MBCC, come in.

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Cyclone detected to the northeast, Force 12. Particulate concentration at 3,500 micrograms per cubic meter. Visibility in the northeast quadrant down to 300 meters. Sandstorm core expected to hit in ten minutes. Over.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Copy. Unable to contact headquarters. Requesting switch to emergency channel.

steps.speaker: Staff C
steps.content: Switching to Channel 112.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Sand Ship 4A calling MBCC. Experiencing high-intensity convection, possible sandstorm. Requesting assistance, do you copy... Dammit! Signal's gone!

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Captain, are we in big trouble?

steps.speaker: Staff C
steps.content: Don't worry, it'll take more than a little gust to sink this ship. But we'll be in real trouble if we get blown off course into dangerous lanes. Now, get yourself below deck. Let's hope our mast can take this!
Milly glances at the tallest mast behind her. It's swaying violently in the wind.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Captain, the mast... Wait, Captain?
But the crew's already gone, and no one else notices the danger she's spotted.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Okay, Milly, calm down. You... you can do this. The storm's not here yet. It's only a few minutes' climb. All you have to do is secure the signal device on the mast. You can't let this ship go down. If it does... you'll never see Chief again.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: You can do this, Milly. Go for it.
With a surge of determination, Milly begins to climb the towering mast.
The air thickens with sand. She feels the coarse grit stinging her face.
Suddenly, the ribbon binding her hair is snatched by the wind, sending her locks whipping in the gale.
Yet in the swirling chaos, her golden hair seems to shimmer, catching the light from colored minerals caught in the strands.
When she finally reaches the crow's nest, the sight before her takes her breath away.
This is the first time she's seen a sandstorm. She's only ever hidden from them in the safety of a cabin; her patrons never talked about such grim things on their trip.
This is her first time witnessing and feeling the raw power of nature.

Chaos presses in. Only the sand ship's stark, white searchlights pierce the dense fog of dust, carving a path forward. But the path reveals only more dark, churning sand and endless dunes, now twisted into unnatural shapes, as if something monstrous is stirring underneath. The hull shudders violently, gravel rattling against the metal in a constant patter.
Milly can no longer hear any other sounds. She trembles before the fury of nature.
She clings to the railing, struggling to keep herself steady. With tremendous effort, she manages to relatch the fallen lock. The swaying mast stabilizes, now secure against the raging sandstorm.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Storm core's hit early. Calling for aid, calling for aid... Dammit, emergency channel's dead too.

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Visibility down to 50 meters. Bridge, kill the engines, recalibrate course. Deploy emergency shields.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Roger that. Hey, Captain! Look! Is that someone out there?! Who in their right mind would be wandering outside in this storm?

steps.speaker: Staff C
steps.content: What the hell, it's the girl. Milly! Get down from there!
Larger pieces of gravel pummel the ship. A rock hits the hull near the mast, shattering a metal part. A shard whizzes past Milly, drawing a thin line of blood.
Milly struggles to climb down, her petite frame swaying precariously in the wind.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Come on, Milly, just a little farther. Don't give up now.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: You worked so hard to see Chief!

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: If you die here, all of it will be for nothing. Chief will never know how you feel, or even remember you!

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: You have to live! You promised! You promised you'd live to see him, and you'd be your best self when you did!
steps.female_content: You have to live! You promised! You promised you'd live to see her, and you'd be your best self when you did!

steps.content: Just as her strength begins to fail, a flashing light pierces the darkness.

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Beacon sighted, northwest quadrant! It's the Bureau!

steps.speaker: Staff C
steps.content: Thank goodness! The brats actually earned their pay for once. I was starting to think they'd clocked out for the day and left us out here to rot. I'll go get Milly. Poor girl must be terrified. If it weren't for her, we'd have lost that mast for sure.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Adjusting coordinates. Northwest, three degrees deviation. That'll take us out of the core of the sandstorm. We're gonna make it!
Guided by the light, the sand ship sails forward. Curiously, the wind on this new course begins to die down, and the ship stops rocking so violently. The storm begins to recede on both sides.
As the storm subsides, Milly's legs finally give out, and she collapses to the ground.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I'm... alive? I'm not... going to die?
The sand ship slowly follows the beacon. Soon, the familiar statues of the DisCity port appear ahead.
[Port at Night]
After the ship docks, Milly finally sees the person who lit the beacon: a young man in a surveyor's uniform with the MBCC logo on it. He vaults onto the deck and greets everyone energetically.

steps.speaker: Young Man
steps.content: Hey! You okay? That was a nasty storm, but it's over now. Can you stand?
He offers Milly a friendly hand.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I'm Kawa-kawa. I heard you guys got lost out there. Are you feeling alright?

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Hello, I... I'm Milly. Did the Bureau send you to get us?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Not exactly. The weather in WhiteSands has been unusual these past few days. I knew some Bureau folks would be returning today, so I came to help guide you in.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: The Bureau doesn't usually assign Sinners to escort duties. Chief just lets me do whatever I want. I have lots of important work in WhiteSands—mapping the terrain, guiding travelers, recording the weather... These are all part of my job.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Your face is bleeding. Must've been a piece of rock in the storm. Here, let me clean it up for you.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Thank you, you're so kind.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Hehe. The sandstorms here are no joke. You're lucky you only got a scratch and didn't get pulled into quicksand.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: But I saw those giant moving sand dunes, like monsters... It was breathtaking.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Wow, you've got guts. Sand dunes are a WhiteSands specialty, but you only see the giant moving ones during a storm.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Perhaps it was the power of love that kept me going. I just kept thinking that I couldn't die there, and I held on... and then I saw them. My legs are still weak just thinking about those dunes.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: The dunes are one side of WhiteSands. But we also have a brilliant starry sky that you won't find anywhere else.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Did you say... stars?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Yep. Especially after a storm, when the sky is perfectly clear.
He points upward and gestures for Milly to look.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: ...Wow.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Chief once told me that the terrifying sand dunes and the beautiful starry sky share the same WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: To see the stars, you just have to be patient. And don't forget to look up.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Don't forget to look up...

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Do you talk to Chief often?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Not really. Chief came to WhiteSands on business once, and I was the guide. It was wild... holy flowers, bandits, sandstorms... you name it. Chief showed up and solved one crisis after another. It was so cool.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: That's a story about Chief I've never heard before. Could you tell me about it?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Huh? Well, I suppose I could. But I'm not much of a storyteller, so...
(End of CG)
Kawa-kawa briefly recounts his adventure with Chief.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: That's so different from the stories I've heard. In my versions, Chief is always a lone hero, charging into enemy lines and single-handedly saving the day. They rarely mentioned Chief's companions.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I... I care for Chief a lot. He's saved me time and time again. I want to tell him how I feel, but whenever I'm in front of him, I get so nervous I can't say a single word.
steps.female_content: I... I care for Chief a lot. She's saved me time and time again. I want to tell her how I feel, but whenever I'm in front of her, I get so nervous I can't say a single word.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Is that why you all do so much for Chief? So Chief will like you and you can talk without getting nervous?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Uh, I don't think you need to go through all that just to talk to Chief.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I guide people in WhiteSands because I love it. I like helping people. Hmm... I guess you're not wrong. Chief is included in "people," after all.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Chief is really nice. He never puts on airs. So you don't need to be so nervous. Honestly, he's the most easy-going person I've ever met. You can tell him anything.
steps.female_content: Chief is really nice. She never puts on airs. So you don't need to be so nervous. Honestly, she's the most easy-going person I've ever met. You can tell her anything.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Alright, my job here is done. I gotta get to my next observation point. Next time you're in WhiteSands, come find me. I'll take you to collect the beacons. You can see all sorts of unique plants and animals along the way. It's a lot of fun.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Hope the rest of your trip goes smoothly. And good luck with Chief! I'll be rooting for you!

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Thank you, Kawa-kawa. I know what to do now.
